facts.fact_text: After the meeting with Mr G.Kh. ended without results, Tbilisi State University employees — including all of the applicants — decided to stay at the University in one of the lecture halls and hold a further meeting among themselves.
On 20 June 2006 the applicants, along with other employees of Tbilisi State University, gathered again in one of the lecture halls of the University.

On 3 July 2006, in response to a request by the fourth applicant, Mr Sanadze, the acting Rector of Tbilisi State University, Mr G.Kh., authorised a meeting of University employees in the Grand Hall of the main University building between 3.30 p.m. and 7 p.m.
At the meeting of 3 July 2006, the already-dissolved Grand Academic Council 'elected' the second applicant as the new Rector of Tbilisi State University.

After the 'election' of the second applicant as new Rector, a group of about twenty people, including all of the applicants, headed to the office of acting Rector Mr G.Kh. to inform him of the Grand Academic Council's decision and to demand his resignation.
According to the applicants, they entered acting Rector Mr G.Kh.'s office on 3 July 2006 without using any force and informed him of the Grand Academic Council's decision.
According to the applicants, they asked Mr G.Kh. to leave his office, but he refused to do so.
According to the applicants, after the police asked the applicants and others present to leave the acting Rector's office, they left without any resistance and moved to a lecture hall.

According to the minutes of the 3 August 2006 hearing, the applicants challenged the factual circumstances of the events of 3 July 2006 as presented by the prosecutor, maintaining that they had not broken into the acting Rector's office but had entered it and sat there calmly without using any force.

According to the minutes of the 3 August 2006 hearing, the applicants maintained that they had not insulted or threatened acting Rector Mr G.Kh. but had simply presented him with the decision of the Grand Academic Council.

According to the minutes of the 3 August 2006 hearing, the applicants maintained that they had not disobeyed the instructions of the police but had left the acting Rector's office within ten or fifteen minutes of being ordered to do so by the police.

At the hearing of 3 August 2006, police patrol officer G.Ch. clarified in reply to a question that no one had physically resisted the police, but that the protesters had simply refused to leave the acting Rector's office.
According to the applicants, at around 1 a.m. on 20 June 2006 the police arrived at Tbilisi State University.
According to the applicants, the police forced everyone out of the Tbilisi State University building without giving any explanations or prior warning.
Towards the evening of 20 June 2006 the police allegedly again dispersed the applicants' meeting at Tbilisi State University.
While the meeting at acting Rector Mr G.Kh.'s office continued, the police entered the Tbilisi State University grounds.
The police officers went directly to the office of acting Rector Mr G.Kh., who immediately left the room upon their arrival.
According to the applicants, after the police asked the applicants and others present to leave the acting Rector's office, they left without any resistance and moved to a lecture hall.
The applicants alleged that at around 11 p.m. on 3 July 2006 the police closed the doors of the lecture hall and prevented the people inside from leaving.
The applicants alleged that they had been locked in the lecture hall without access to water, food or toilet facilities until approximately 8-10 a.m. on 4 July 2006.

Article 9(1) of the Law of Georgia on Assembly and Demonstrations, as worded at the material time, prohibited holding an assembly or a demonstration inside the building of the Parliament of Georgia, the residency of the President of Georgia, the Constitutional Court and the Supreme Court of Georgia, on the premises of courts, prosecutor's offices or of police, penitentiary or military units and sites, in railway stations, airports, hospitals or diplomatic missions (or within a 20-metre radius thereof), on the premises of governmental institutions or local self-government bodies, or in the buildings of companies, institutions and organisations that operate under special labour security rules or are under armed guard.

Article 1(3) of the Law of Georgia on Assembly and Demonstrations, as worded at the material time, provided that the law sets out the requirement that the authorities be notified if an assembly or a demonstration is due to be held in a public place or a place through which transport passes.

Under Article 9 of the Law on the Police, as in force at the material time, the police were responsible inter alia for dispersing unlawful rallies, demonstrations, pickets and other assemblies that posed a threat to public safety, the lives and health of people, property, and other rights guaranteed by law.

Article 1(1) of the Law of Georgia on Assembly and Demonstrations, as worded at the material time, provided that the law regulates the exercise of the right guaranteed by the Constitution of Georgia to gather publicly, unarmed, both indoors and outdoors, without prior permission.
According to the applicants, despite the applicants' repeated requests, the police officers did not show them any order authorising the removal of the people gathered at Tbilisi State University.

According to the Government's official version of events, the Tbilisi State University security service was no longer in control of the situation and the functioning of the University administration was disrupted.
According to the Government's official version of events, the police were called to restore order because the applicants and other protesters were refusing to leave.
According to the Imedi video recording of 3 July 2006, dozens of protesters had simultaneously gathered in the corridor adjacent to the acting Rector's office and had chanted 'step down!'

At the press briefing on 4 July 2006, the Minister of Education of Georgia stated: 'Those people, who went beyond all the limits of academia and ethics yesterday, will of course, face responsibility for that.'

Under Article 9 of the Law on the Police, as in force at the material time, the police were responsible inter alia for dispersing unlawful rallies, demonstrations, pickets and other assemblies that posed a threat to public safety, the lives and health of people, property, and other rights guaranteed by law.
According to the applicants, at around 1 a.m. on 20 June 2006 the police arrived at Tbilisi State University.
According to the applicants, the police forced everyone out of the Tbilisi State University building without giving any explanations or prior warning.
The applicants alleged that at around 11 p.m. on 3 July 2006 the police closed the doors of the lecture hall and prevented the people inside from leaving.
The applicants alleged that they had been locked in the lecture hall without access to water, food or toilet facilities until approximately 8-10 a.m. on 4 July 2006.
The applicants were served with a copy of the prosecutor's ruling of 29 July 2006 late in the evening of 29 July 2006.
At the hearing of 30 July 2006, the applicants complained that they had not had sufficient time to acquaint themselves with the relevant material in the case file and to hire a lawyer.

At the 3 August 2006 hearing, the applicants tried to put several questions to the prosecutor regarding the alleged locking in the lecture hall, but the presiding judge dismissed the questions as irrelevant and having no bearing on the case.

As shown in Imedi's recording of the events of 3 July 2006, at least twenty people had entered the reception area of acting Rector Mr G.Kh.'s office by force, in disregard of the protests of the security staff and reception staff.

As shown in Imedi's recording of the events of 3 July 2006, some of those who entered the reception area had walked into the acting Rector's office itself, notifying Mr G.Kh. of the decision of the Grand Academic Council and demanding his resignation.
According to the Imedi video recording of 3 July 2006, dozens of protesters had simultaneously gathered in the corridor adjacent to the acting Rector's office and had chanted 'step down!'

At the press briefing on 4 July 2006, the Minister of Education of Georgia stated: 'Those people, who went beyond all the limits of academia and ethics yesterday, will of course, face responsibility for that.'

In connection with the charge of a minor breach of public order (minor hooliganism), the Tbilisi City Court established that the applicants had burst into the office of acting Rector Mr G.Kh., calling for his resignation.
The Tbilisi City Court established that the applicants had demanded, in an insulting manner, that acting Rector Mr G.Kh. immediately leave his office and take all his belongings with him.

The Tbilisi City Court concluded that the applicants had occupied the office of acting Rector Mr G.Kh. against his will for about two hours and had disregarded his repeated requests for them to leave.

The Tbilisi City Court concluded that the applicants' behaviour had amounted to insulting harassment with respect to Mr G.Kh. and other staff present, and to 'other similar action' that had violated public order and peace.

In the ruling of 29 July 2006, the prosecutor also decided to terminate proceedings that had apparently been opened against police officers in respect of their alleged unlawful use of force on 3-4 July 2006, finding the complaint lodged by the applicants in that connection unsubstantiated.
The applicants were served with a copy of the prosecutor's ruling of 29 July 2006 late in the evening of 29 July 2006.
At the hearing of 30 July 2006, the applicants complained that they had not had sufficient time to acquaint themselves with the relevant material in the case file and to hire a lawyer.

At the 3 August 2006 hearing, the applicants tried to put several questions to the prosecutor regarding the alleged locking in the lecture hall, but the presiding judge dismissed the questions as irrelevant and having no bearing on the case.

At the hearing of 3 August 2006, V.J., a member of the Tbilisi State University security service, claimed that about fifty people — disregarding his orders and pushing him away — had forced their way to the reception area of the acting Rector's office.
At the hearing of 3 August 2006, police patrol officer G.Ch. stated that he had entered the University building and tried to enter the acting Rector's office, which had been blocked by protesters.
At the hearing of 3 August 2006, police patrol officer G.Ch. stated that it had taken him and the other officers about one hour to persuade the protesters to leave the acting Rector's office.

At the hearing of 3 August 2006, police officer Z.S. confirmed that while no force had been used, the police had spent an hour persuading a group of about twenty people to leave the acting Rector's office.

At the hearing of 3 August 2006, police officer Z.S. stated that the second applicant, Mr Mebonia, had been taken out of the acting Rector's office still sitting on a chair as he had refused to stand up and leave by himself.

The two journalists and two professors questioned on 3 August 2006 claimed that the group had been simply demanding the resignation of Mr G.Kh. and that they had left the office at the request of the police.
